blockers:
- Open, N1 (validated by trace). A program word with an expansion in it is not denied unless a later word is literally `commit` or `push`. In writesOf, shell.ts 511-515, the `UNREADABLE` program test also requires `words.slice(start + 1).some(w => w === "commit" || w === "push")`. Each of these returns [] while the `if` glob still matches the text. `git${IFS}commit${IFS}-m${IFS}x` is one word, so nothing follows it. `{git,commit,-m,x}` is brace expansion, one word. `g=git c=commit; $g $c -m x` and `$(echo git) $(echo commit) -m x` work the same way. The inner `echo git` is a separate command, and the outer program `$()` has only `$()` after it. `bash -c '"$@"' _ git commit -m x`, `sh -c '$1' _ 'git commit -m x'` and `sh -c '$0 $1' git commit` are single-quoted, so shellWrites sees no EXPANDED mark in the script. The script's own command is `$@` with no literal commit after it, and the outer words are never read. Impact: an unreviewed `git commit` with no `vcs commit` redirect. The docs claim `$g commit` and `git $p` are denied, but the denial depends on the literal word. Fix: deny any command whose program word is UNREADABLE, or contains `{`, `$` or a backtick; a bare `$()` as program is the same. If the hook only starts on git-plus-commit text, this costs nothing.
- Open, N2 (validated by trace; depends on bash's `((` fallback, about 80% sure). The new `((` skip (shell.ts 248-263) counts parens from the first `(`. `((git commit) && (true))` skips to the final `))`, contains no `;`, `$(`, backtick, quote, backslash or newline, and ends with `))`, so `unclear` is not set and the commands are never scanned. Bash's parse_arith_cmd reads from the second `(` to the first matching `)`. The next character is a space, not `)`, so bash falls back to two nested subshells and runs `git commit`. Same for `((git push -f) && (true))`. Closes B5 only for `$(` and backticks. Fix: skip `((` only if the first `)` that closes the inner paren is immediately followed by `)`. Otherwise scan it as code, or set unclear.
- Open, N3 (validated by trace). Command-position forms that writesOf does not follow, each returning [] while the `if` glob matches. `time -p git commit -m x`: `time` is a keyword, then `-p` breaks the loop and is read as the program. `/usr/bin/time git commit -m x` is not recognized as the keyword and is not in WRAPPERS. `coproc git commit -m x` and `coproc N { git commit -m x; }`. `function f { git commit -m x; }; f`: the words are `function f { git commit ...`, so the program is `function`; only the `f() {` form reaches `{`. `trap 'git commit -m x' EXIT`. `source /dev/stdin <<< 'git commit -m x'` and `. <(echo 'git commit -m x')` (`source` and `.` are not in RUNNERS). `fakeroot git commit -m x`, `mise exec -- git commit -m x`, `pkexec`, `docker exec c git commit`, `bwrap`, `faketime`, and any other prefix not in WRAPPERS or RUNNERS. `xargs git < <(echo commit)`: with no subcommand, `if (subcommand === undefined) return []` (shell.ts 525) passes it. `echo 'git commit -m x' | xargs -I{} sh -c '{}'`: the script is `{}`, which reads as nothing. Fix: a denylist of wrappers cannot be completed. Scan every non-first word that is `git` or ends in `/git` as an embedded invocation unless the program is a known reader (echo, printf, cat, grep, …). Treat a missing git subcommand, and an `sh -c` script that is only a placeholder, as unclear. Add `time`, `coproc`, `function`, `trap`, `source`, `.`, `at` and `batch` to the command-position handling.
- Open, N4 (validated by trace). Wrapper and shell option misparse. `env -iS 'git commit -m x'`: the -S check at shell.ts 499 matches only a word that starts with -S, so the cluster `-iS` is skipped as a flag and the quoted string becomes the program. `timeout .5 git commit -m x`, and `timeout inf git commit -m x`: afterWrapper accepts only a duration that starts with a digit. `bash -c -x 'git commit -m x'` and `sh -c -- 'git commit -m x'`: bash takes the first non-option word after -c as the script, but shellWrites uses words[flag + 1], which is `-x` or `--`, and returns []. Fix: for `-c` use the first following word that does not start with `-` and is not `--`; match `-S` anywhere in an env option cluster; treat any duration-like word as the timeout duration.
- Open, N5 (validated by trace; bash `${…}` and subscript arithmetic about 80% sure). `<<` inside `${x:1<<2 }` or `a[1<<2 ]=1` is arithmetic in bash, but the scanner opens a heredoc. The delimiter `2` is delimiter-shaped, since the space ends the word. With a later line `2`, the heredoc closes, nothing in the body trips unclear, and the body is skipped. Command: line 1 `echo ${x:1<<2 }`, line 2 `git commit -m x`, line 3 `2`. Bash runs line 2 and then fails on `2`. A closing `}` or `]` attached to the delimiter, as in `${a[1<<2]}`, is already unclear, so only the spaced form passes. B3 is closed for `$[`, `((` and `for ((`, but this shape remains. Fix: track `${` and `a[` context, or set unclear when a heredoc body is skipped and its text has a `git` word followed by `commit` or `push`.
- Open, N6 (validated; alias class, lower weight). The `GIT_CONFIG*` check runs only on words at the start of a command or after an env, wrapper or assignment prefix (shell.ts 494-498). `export GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=alias.ci GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=commit; git ci -m x # git commit` returns [] (`export` is the program). `git config alias.ci commit; git ci -m x` also passes, because `git config` is not a write. The agent defines the alias itself, not the user's config. Both are close to the documented `.git/` edit residual, so the root may accept them, but the docs list `GIT_CONFIG*` and `-c alias.*` as denied while these two routes stay open. Fix: scan every word of every command for `^GIT_(CONFIG|ALIAS)`, and treat `git config` with `alias.*` or `remote.*.push` as unclear.
notes:
- Closed with reason: B1 CLOSED. A decoded NUL in `$'…'` sets unclear (scanAnsiC, shell.ts 196); `\0`, `\x00` and the octal form all decode to U+0000. B2 CLOSED. An unquoted heredoc whose body holds `$(` or a backtick, or that never closes, sets unclear (skipHeredocs 51-67); `<<'EOF'` and `<<\EOF` stay readable. B4 CLOSED. scanDouble drops backslash plus newline (109-112), so `git "com\<nl>mit"` reads as commit. B3 PARTLY CLOSED. `$[` and `((` anywhere are now unclear or skipped, an unterminated heredoc or a non-delimiter word after `<<` is unclear, and `<<<` is a redirect. The `${x:1<<2 }` shape is open (N5). B5 PARTLY CLOSED. `$(`, a backtick, `;`, a quote or a newline inside `((…))` is unclear, but the nested-subshell reading is open (N2).
- Wrapper, alias and dynamic-subcommand shapes: nested backticks now unclear (shell.ts 270). eval, setsid, stdbuf, ionice, flock, ssh, su, watch, parallel and the rest of RUNNERS are unclear. `find -exec/-execdir/-ok/-okdir` unclear. A shell with no script file, `-s`, a pipe or a heredoc is unclear. `fish`, `csh`, `ash` are in SHELLS. `env -S` and `--split-string` are unclear, only for the plain `-S` spelling (N4). `git $p`, `git -c alias.*`, `-c remote.*.push=` and `.mirror=`, `-c push.*`, `--config-env` and `--attr-source` are unclear. `GIT_CONFIG*` as a command prefix is unclear. Residual stays open: include files named by `-c include.path=/tmp/x` that define an alias, which equals the documented `.git/` and script residual. Inline interpreters (`python -c`, `node -e`, `perl -e`) that spawn git also stay open, as scripts that run git inside.
- commit-msg changes (hook.ts 144-166, 277-299): `fileSetting` uses `git config --show-origin --get` and drops any value whose origin starts with `command line:`, which covers `-c`, GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS and GIT_CONFIG_COUNT. Sound. Still open and non-blocking, policy only: the phrase check skips everything below an exact scissors line, so `git commit -m $'x\n<comment> ------------------------ >8 ------------------------\nthe user asked …'` keeps the phrase in the commit. Attribution is stripped there but phrases are not checked. The `#` comment lines also stay unchecked for phrases (the earlier V5). `vcs commit` checks the full text, so only a commit that got past the redirect is affected.
- S1 still unverified: I could not check whether the `Bash(*git*commit*)` and `Bash(*git*push*)` `if` globs match a multi-line command. Several shapes above need a newline, and a command that is not matched never reaches the hook.
- Fail-closed handling in hook.ts 247-258 is sound. Any exception from gitWrites becomes `unclear` and a deny, and `onFailure` is block. The `unclear` REDIRECTS text matches what the scanner now denies. A deny cannot stop a command with no git write, so the over-deny cost is limited to commands whose text has git and then commit or push.
- Plain `git push`, `gh pr create --body-file - <<'EOF'` with a quoted heredoc, and `bash script.sh` still pass, as the tests show. The new tests cover B1 to B5 and the listed wrapper and alias shapes but none of N1 to N6.
